description: Issue #1178: the shared corpus for the registry snapshot contract, docs/contracts/registry-snapshot.json: its shape, its code rules N1-N3, and its snapshot digest. Every package that reads or writes a registry snapshot is tested against every case here. digests holds valid snapshots with the canonical JSON of each one's digest subject and its expected digest; invalid holds snapshots every reader must refuse, with the rule ('schema' for the contract's keywords, else the code rule's id) and the position of each violation. The expected canonical strings and digests were produced independently of any package: a stand-alone Python 3 script built each subject from the contract's prose (registry, and each package's name, status, latest and versions, packages sorted by name and each package's versions sorted by version), serialized it with json.dumps(subject, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')) -- which is RFC 8785 for these values, because every key and every sorted string is ASCII (so code-point order equals UTF-16 order) and the subject holds no number -- and hashed its UTF-8 bytes with hashlib.sha256. The integrity values are sha512 hashes of made-up text, not of any real tarball, and the responseSha256 values hash made-up text too.

digests.name: base
digests.note: Three packages, each found, with latest naming its one recorded version. The packages are written out of name order.

digests.name: base-refetched
digests.note: base fetched again later by a newer fetcher: fetchedAt, fetchedBy, every responseSha256 and the package order differ. Same digest as base.

digests.name: two-versions
digests.note: base with a second, older writer version recorded after the one latest names.

digests.name: two-versions-reordered
digests.note: two-versions with writer's versions written in the other order. Same digest as two-versions.

digests.name: change-registry
digests.note: base with another registry. A different digest.

digests.name: change-latest
digests.note: base with writer's latest naming a version the snapshot does not record. A different digest.

digests.name: change-version
digests.note: base with writer's latest and its version entry both 0.4.2, everything else kept. A different digest.

digests.name: change-integrity
digests.note: base with another integrity value for writer. A different digest.

digests.name: change-tarball
digests.note: base with another tarball URL for writer. A different digest.

digests.name: change-deprecated
digests.note: base with writer's version deprecated. A different digest.

digests.name: change-published-at
digests.note: base with another publish time for writer. A different digest.

digests.name: change-attestations
digests.note: base with writer listing no attestations. A different digest.

digests.name: change-status
digests.note: base with designer not found. A different digest.

digests.name: change-name
digests.note: base with designer's entry naming another package. A different digest.

digests.name: odd-but-valid
digests.note: A snapshot that is valid in shape but that a resolver refuses: a prerelease latest, a sha1-only integrity value, no latest at all, a null publish time, and no integrity value.

invalid.name: n3-not-found-with-latest-and-versions
invalid.note: designer not found, yet with a latest and a version.

invalid.name: schema-unknown-top-level-field
invalid.note: An undeclared top-level field, reported at the document, never by its name.

snapshot.founderNote: text that must never be quoted

invalid.name: schema-unknown-version-field
invalid.note: An undeclared field in a version entry, reported at that entry, never by its name.

invalid.name: schema-http-registry
invalid.note: A registry that is not https.

invalid.name: schema-registry-with-path
invalid.note: A registry with a trailing slash.

invalid.name: schema-latest-not-a-version
invalid.note: latest holding a dist-tag name, not a version.

invalid.name: schema-deprecation-message
invalid.note: deprecated holding the registry's message instead of true.

invalid.name: schema-bad-fetch-time
invalid.note: A fetch time that is not a real date-time.
